nodes.content: Design a multi-tenant workflow runtime enforcing information-flow isolation across shared caches, asynchronous retries, and explicitly authorized declassification.
requirements: Establish termination-insensitive noninterference under concurrent execution and retries, except for tenant-authorized declassification.
Keep median workflow latency overhead below 15% versus identical executions without information-flow enforcement.

nodes.content: Implement tenant-scoped dynamic labels, label-keyed caches, label-preserving retry envelopes, versioned declassification capabilities, and memoized label joins.
How can shared-cache eviction and retry scheduling avoid secret-dependent changes to tenant-visible outputs under concurrent execution?
Per-label cache quotas and reserved retry lanes preserve low-output traces across high-input variants at under 15% median overhead.
Implement per-label cache quotas and reserved retry lanes; compare paired secret-variant traces modulo authorized releases and measure median overhead.
Run FlowPair-10k concurrent secret-variant schedules with evictions and retries; compare low traces modulo authorized releases and median latency against baseline.
FlowPair-10k found 31/10,000 low-trace mismatches: cross-label eviction changed visible retry status; median latency overhead was 12%.
Hard-partitioned cache capacity and label-local retry status eliminate cross-label trace mismatches while retaining under 15% median overhead.
Rerun FlowPair-10k concurrent schedules with hard-partitioned cache capacity and label-local retry status; compare release-normalized traces and baseline-relative median overhead.
FlowPair-10k rerun found 0/10,000 release-normalized low-trace mismatches with hard partitions and label-local retry status; median overhead was 13.4%.
Adopt hard-partitioned caches and label-local retry status over quotas: mismatches fell from 31 to zero at 13.4% overhead.
Implement the quota-cache and reserved-retry-lane baseline; compare paired traces and median overhead against adopted partitions on FlowPair-10k.
FlowPair-10k harness and comparison report document quota versus partition results: 31 versus zero trace mismatches, 12% versus 13.4% median overhead.
How do quota-based caches and reserved retry lanes compare with hard partitions on low-trace isolation and median latency?
Use tenant-signed, audience-scoped release capabilities with replay-safe retry binding, one-time verification, and auditable declassification events.
Prove release-aware trace equivalence across cache and retry interleavings; implement idempotent capability consumption and benchmark median overhead below 15%.
Extend FlowPair-10k with capability replay and audience-mismatch cases; enumerate cache/retry interleavings and measure release-normalized mismatches and median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1 contains replay and audience-mismatch fixtures, an interleaving enumerator, release-normalized trace checker, and median-overhead report.
Run FlowPair-10k-Release v1 on partitioned caches and signed capabilities under concurrent retries; measure unauthorized releases, trace mismatches, median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1 found 0 unauthorized releases or low-trace mismatches in 10,000 cases; join-cache invalidations raised median overhead to 16.8%.
Retain hard partitions and signed release capabilities; defer deployment until join-cache invalidation overhead drops below 15%.
Benchmark quota-based caches with reserved retry lanes against hard partitions on FlowPair-10k-Release v1, comparing trace mismatches and median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1: quotas had 37/10,000 low-trace mismatches at 14.3% median overhead; partitions had zero at 16.8%.
Can capability-versioned, tenant-local label-join caches reduce invalidation costs without admitting revoked releases or exceeding 15% median overhead?
Partitions had zero mismatches at 16.8%; tenant-local epoch-keyed joins should avoid invalidations, save ≥1.9 points, and block revocation leaks.
Implement tenant-local epoch-keyed join caches; replay revocation races in FlowPair-10k-Release v1 and measure unauthorized releases, trace mismatches, median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1 found 2 revoked-capability releases in 10,000 revocation races despite 14.4% median overhead.
Tenant-local epoch-keyed joins plus atomic revocation-epoch validation at release commit eliminate revoked releases while maintaining median overhead below 15%.
Add atomic epoch checks at release commit; repeat revocation-race tests and compare mismatches and overhead against partition and cached-join baselines.
Implement atomic epoch-check-and-consume at release commit; rerun FlowPair-10k-Release v1 revocation races, measuring revoked releases, low-trace mismatches, and median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1 found zero revoked releases or low-trace mismatches in 10,000 races; median overhead was 14.7%.
Adopt hard partitions over quotas, tenant-local epoch-keyed joins, and atomic release checks: zero mismatches and revoked releases at 14.7% overhead.
Develop a per-tenant stuttering-simulation proof for release-aware noninterference across cache/retry interleavings, alongside epoch-check cost accounting.
Model concurrent cache, retry, and release steps; prove termination-insensitive tenant-low equivalence modulo authorized releases; benchmark median overhead below 15%.
Encode FlowPair-10k-Release v1 cache, retry, and release semantics in TLA+; model-check paired low traces across interleavings.
FlowIso.tla defines paired-tenant executions, partitioned caches, label-local retries, atomic release checks, and release-normalized low-trace assertions.
Run TLC on FlowIso.tla with three tenants, two retries, and revocation; check release-normalized stuttering equivalence across interleavings.
TLC explored 1.2 million FlowIso states with three tenants, two retries, and revocation; no release-normalized low-trace violations occurred.
What inductive relation proves release-normalized low-trace equivalence for unbounded retries and tenant counts beyond TLC's three-tenant model?
Equal tenant-low cache and retry projections with aligned authorized-release ledgers form an inductive stuttering relation for unbounded tenants and retries.
Check FlowIso.tla in TLAPS for parametric initialization, cache, retry, revocation, release preservation, and low-step matching under the proposed relation.
TLAPS found paired states satisfying cache/retry projections and release-ledger alignment, but differing pending low notifications violate step matching.
Replay TLAPS counterexample in FlowIso.tla and test whether pending-notification equality restores low-step matching for the proposed relation.
FlowIso replay traced notification divergence to unreachable queue states; reachable retry transitions preserved n40’s low projections and matched notifications.
Strengthen n40’s relation with reachable-queue equality for pending low notifications; defer the unbounded proof until TLAPS verifies it.
Use tenant-partitioned notification outboxes with atomic retry/release commits, a TLAPS queue invariant, and a 15% median-overhead CI gate.
Does atomic outbox insertion preserve pending-notification equality through crashes and replayed retries without exceeding 15% median latency overhead?
Atomic retry/release commits to tenant-partitioned outboxes with retry-ID deduplication preserve pending-notification equality after crashes below 15% median overhead.
Implement atomic retry/release commits to tenant-partitioned outboxes with retry-ID deduplication; TLAPS-check queue equality, fault-inject crash replays, benchmark median overhead.
Fault-inject 10,000 crash/replay pairs into FlowPair-10k-Release v1 outboxes; compare pending queues and low traces, benchmark median overhead.
FlowPair-10k-Release v1 crash/replay runs showed zero pending-queue or low-trace mismatches in 10,000 pairs; median overhead was 14.8%.
Encode the crash-tested outbox commits in FlowIso.tla and use TLAPS to prove pending-notification equality for unbounded retry sequences.
FlowIso-Outbox.tla contains atomic commit semantics, retry-ID deduplication, and TLAPS lemmas preserving paired pending-notification equality.
Run TLAPS on FlowIso-Outbox.tla to verify n45’s strengthened queue relation and parametric release-aware stuttering; rerun 15% overhead gate.
TLAPS discharged 23/23 parametric release-aware stuttering obligations; FlowPair-10k-Release v1 measured 14.8% median overhead.
Lift proof deferral and adopt tenant-partitioned atomic outboxes: TLAPS discharged 23/23 obligations, with 14.8% median overhead.
Enforce proof-to-code conformance with transition-level runtime assertions, tenant-isolated audit logs, and a sub-15% median-overhead deployment gate.
Instrument cache, retry, release, and outbox transitions against FlowIso-Outbox.tla; fuzz tenant-paired executions and enforce a <15% median-overhead CI gate.
Map runtime cache, retry, release, and outbox events to FlowIso-Outbox.tla actions; add assertions for labels, epochs, and outbox deduplication.
FlowIso-Guard v1 maps runtime events to FlowIso-Outbox.tla actions and asserts label partitions, release epochs, and retry-ID deduplication.
Fuzz FlowIso-Guard v1 across 10,000 paired revocation, eviction, and crash schedules; check assertions, unauthorized releases, traces, and median overhead.
FlowIso-Guard v1 passed 10,000 paired schedules with zero assertion failures, unauthorized releases, or trace mismatches; median overhead was 14.9%.
Can shared audit-log batching expose cross-tenant release activity through tenant-visible receipts or push median overhead past 15%?
Tenant-scoped receipt sequences and asynchronous per-tenant audit batching hide cross-tenant releases while keeping median overhead below 15%.
Extend FlowIso-Guard v1 with tenant-scoped receipts and audit batches; fuzz cross-tenant releases, comparing receipt traces and median overhead.
FlowIso-Guard v1 found 8/10,000 cross-tenant receipt-trace mismatches: shared flush acknowledgments exposed batch occupancy; median overhead was 14.9%.
Retain partitioned caches, epoch-checked releases, and atomic outboxes; block deployment until tenant-local audit acknowledgments eliminate receipt leaks.
